title: Paradise Alley and meeting Yusef Lateef
summary: The St. Antoine and Adams clubs where saxophonists jammed, and where he taught Yusef Lateef (then Bill Evans) his first chord changes.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: But anyway, getting back to the music. Down in Paradise Alley, that's where the action was. The Turf Club was there on St. Antoine. They had the D&C across the street, where we used to go over there and jam. And they had some very well-known saxophone players who used to play around there. A guy named Moon Mullins and his partner Lamont, and Larry DeVito, a very fine Italian tenor saxophone player, who was really a great player.

In fact, this place is where I first met Yusef Lateef. Now, his name was Bill Evans at the time. In fact, I taught him... I was the first guy to teach him the chord changes to a song. It was "Coquette", "My Little Coquette." Yeah...

And there were so many great players around there. And on Hastings Street, they... That was about a block over from St. Antoine. Adams was the main vein, going east and west. They had the big Plantation...
[END OF TAPE 2, SIDE A, AT #449 ON COUNTER]
...Club on Adams Boulevard, which I worked later when it became the Plantation -- I will talk about that after a while.
